title: Beyond Accuracy: The Role of Calibration in Self-Improving Large Language Models
extended_summary:
This preprint examines whether iterative self-improvement in large language models introduces bias in confidence estimation, especially overconfidence, and how calibration methods can be combined with self-improvement to improve reliability. The paper frames two main questions: whether self-improvement causes confidence-estimation bias, and what happens when calibration is applied before, after, or during repeated self-improvement steps.

The authors study three self-improvement paradigms: basic prompting, chain-of-thought prompting, and supervised fine-tuning. They evaluate these approaches using open-source LLMs (Llama-2-7b-chat-hf and DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B) on the MMLU benchmark. They also test three ways of combining calibration with self-improvement: iterative calibration after each round, calibration before self-improvement, and calibration after multiple rounds of self-improvement. Outcomes are model accuracy and expected calibration error (ECE), with confidence distributions examined across rounds.

This is not an education study and includes no K-12 learners, teachers, or instructional writing context. The population is language models evaluated on a benchmark dataset rather than human participants in schools. No classroom implementation, teacher mediation, writing instruction, revision support, or feedback intervention for students is studied.

The main conclusion is that iterative self-improvement tends to increase overconfidence, reflected in worsening calibration and rising ECE across rounds, even when accuracy may sometimes improve. Applying calibration after self-improvement most effectively reduces ECE, while calibration before self-improvement can provide a stronger starting point for stronger models. Overall, the paper contributes methodological insight about reliability and calibration in self-improving LLMs, not evidence about generative AI writing support in K-12 education.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a preprint under review in computer science, not a K-12 education study. It contains no student participants, no educational writing intervention, and no school-based empirical design relevant to the requested evidence base.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports model calibration and accuracy outcomes on MMLU benchmark tasks, not learner literacy or writing outcomes. It therefore provides no direct evidence of impact for K-12 generative AI writing, revision, or feedback interventions.
